messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: How to order geom_bar?
parts:
reorder() works globally in reordering levels of a factor, not
locally. In other words, you can reorder the bars once for the levels
of the dodging factor, but you can't reorder them separately for each
value of Regiao. Here's a reproducible example:

d <- data.frame(f1 = factor(rep(LETTERS[1:3], each = 3)),
f2 = factor(rep(c("I", "II", "III"), 3)),
ct = c(10, 15, 20, 16, 14, 12, 18, 13, 20))

library(ggplot2)

# default bar plot
ggplot(d, aes(x = f1, y = ct, fill = f2)) +
geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge")

# reorder the levels of the second factor by count
ggplot(d, aes(x = f1, y = ct, fill = reorder(f2, ct))) +
geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge")

It chooses the order II, I, III because the total count in I is 44, 42
in II and 54 in III. Notice that the ordering of the dodged bars is
the same across all levels of the factor on the horizontal axis.

What you want is to be able to reorder the levels of an 'inner' factor
conditional on the levels of the 'outer' factor. AFAIK there is no
simple way to satisfy your request. One thought is to take the
interaction of the two factors and define the levels of the second
factor according to increasing count within the levels of the first
factor, but then you'd destroy the spacing between the levels of
Regiao. You would also have to adjust the x-axis labels with a scale
function. Here's a first stab at it:

# Hack job on defining the levels of the interaction factor
d$f12 <- with(d, factor(interaction(f1, f2), levels =
c("A.I", "A.II", "A.III", "B.III", "B.II", "B.I", "C.II", "C.I", "C.III")))

ggplot(d, aes(f12, ct, fill = f2)) +
geom_bar(stat = "identity")

My guess is that to do this right, you'd need to use grid graphics
directly unless there's some way to do it with the gtable package, but
that's beyond my current knowledge base. Perhaps one or more of the
ggplot2 gurus can be of assistance.

Dennis
